title: A Thermodynamic Theory of Learning Part II: History-Dependent Reachability and Continual Learning
abstract: arXiv:2602.07950v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We formulate plasticity as target-dependent, finite-horizon reachability under history-dependent dynamics, using standard minimum-energy control theory. An extended state includes parameters and internal variables that affect future updates. Around a reference trajectory, the input-to-endpoint response and its controllability Gramian determine the minimum input energy for each reachable displacement. Minimizing this energy over the joint task target defines a task-conditioned adaptation cost, exact for the arbitrary-input linear model. A solvable learning-retention example shows that this cost can increase without any rank loss, and distinguishes small directional gain from an inaccessible direction. Wasserstein transport supplies a complementary global lower bound, while learning-map Jacobians describe deformation of initial perturbations rather than response to future inputs. tldr: 该论文将神经可塑性建模为依赖历史动力学下的最小能量可达性问题，提出任务条件化的适应代价理论，证明了学习代价可在不发生秩损失的情况下持续增长，从而为持续学习中学习与记忆保持之间的权衡提供了理论刻画。
en_tdlr: This paper formulates plasticity as target-dependent, finite-horizon reachability under history-dependent dynamics using minimum-energy control theory, defines a task-conditioned adaptation cost that can increase without any rank loss, and thereby theoretically characterizes the learning-retention frontier in continual learning.
